text:
# SEO and GEO audit: atlas-roadmaps

I read all 10 tracked files. The site is a small Remix app with 5 routes. `geo.config.json` sets the intended policy: allow AI search crawlers, block training crawlers. I checked each finding against that policy. I haven't run the app, so these come from the source alone.

## High severity

**1. `public/robots.txt:5-6` blocks Bingbot.**
- Bing is the index behind Bing, Copilot, and ChatGPT search results, and DuckDuckGo also draws on it. Blocking it removes the site from all of those.
- It contradicts `geo.config.json` (`aiSearchCrawlers: "allow"`).
- Fix: delete the Bingbot block.

**2. `app/routes/changelog.tsx:4-6` renders its content only on the client.**
- `entries` starts as `[]` and is filled by `useEffect` + `fetch('/api/changelog')`. The server-rendered HTML therefore contains just an empty `<ul>`.
- Most AI crawlers don't run JavaScript, so the changelog is invisible to them. Google may also index it late or not at all.
- No `/api/changelog` route exists in the repo, so it may not work at all.
- Fix: add a Remix `loader` that returns the entries and read them with `useLoaderData()`.

**3. `app/routes/pricing.tsx:1` has no `meta` export and no concrete pricing.**
- With no `meta`, the page has no title, description, or canonical URL. It will fall back to the root title "Atlas".
- The body says "Talk to us for a quote". There are no plans, prices, or comparison, which is what answer engines look for when asked "how much does Atlas cost?".
- Fix: export `meta` with a title, description, and canonical. Add real tiers and prices as HTML text, plus `Product`/`Offer` JSON-LD.

## Medium severity

**4. `public/robots.txt:8-9` only blocks GPTBot, so the training-crawler policy isn't enforced.**
- `geo.config.json` says to block training crawlers, but only GPTBot is blocked.
- ClaudeBot, anthropic-ai, Google-Extended, CCBot, Applebot-Extended, Bytespider, and similar crawlers fall under `User-agent: *` and are allowed.
- Fix: add `Disallow: /` groups for those user agents.
- Optionally, add explicit `Allow: /` groups for the search and retrieval crawlers: OAI-SearchBot, ChatGPT-User, PerplexityBot, Claude-SearchBot, and Claude-User. They are already allowed by default, but explicit groups prevent regressions.

**5. `public/robots.txt` has no `Sitemap:` line.**
- Fix: add `Sitemap: https://atlasroadmaps.example/sitemap.xml`.

**6. `app/root.tsx:2` has a generic title and no site-wide defaults.**
- The title is just "Atlas" and the description is generic.
- There is no `og:title`, `og:description`, `og:image`, `og:type`, `twitter:card`, or `viewport` meta.
- Any route without its own `meta` (currently `/pricing`) inherits this.
- Fix: add a viewport tag and Open Graph/Twitter defaults in the root `meta`.

**7. No structured data anywhere.**
- Fix: add `Organization` and `WebSite` JSON-LD in `app/root.tsx`. Add `SoftwareApplication` on `app/routes/_index.tsx`, `Product`/`Offer` on pricing, and `FAQPage` where a FAQ exists.

**8. `app/routes/_index.tsx:9` uses a `<div onClick>` for its main internal link.**
- Crawlers don't follow `navigate()` calls, and a div isn't keyboard-accessible.
- Fix: replace it with `<Link to="/features">See all features</Link>`.
- Nothing links to `/features` from the root nav (`app/root.tsx:7`), so this div is the only path to it. Add Features and Home links to the nav too.

## Low severity

**9. `app/routes/_index.tsx:8` makes a vague, unsupported claim.**
- "Integrates with all the tools you already use" names no integrations, so there is nothing for an AI answer to quote or cite.
- Fix: list the actual integrations by name, for example "Integrates with Jira, GitHub, Slack, and Linear" (whichever are true).

**10. `app/routes/features.tsx:1` has thin content.**
- It is one sentence ("Timelines, sharing and status updates") under an `<h1>`.
- Fix: give each feature its own `<h2>` and a short, factual description, written so a section can stand alone as an answer.

**11. `public/sitemap.xml:3-6` has no `<lastmod>`.**
- Fix: add `<lastmod>` to each URL. Generate the file from routes rather than keeping it hand-written, so it stays accurate.

**12. `public/robots.txt:3` disallows `/dashboard`, while `app/routes/dashboard.tsx:1` also sets `noindex`.**
- Crawlers blocked by robots.txt never fetch the page, so they never see the `noindex`. The URL can still show up in results without a snippet.
- This is fine for a private area. If you want the URL fully out of the index, remove the `Disallow` and rely on `noindex`.

**13. No `llms.txt` in `public/`.**
- It's optional and its effect is unproven. A short file describing the site and linking to key pages is cheap to add.

## What's already fine
- `<html lang="en">` is set (`app/root.tsx:4`).
- Each page except pricing has one `<h1>`.
- Canonicals are present and correct on `/`, `/features`, and `/changelog`.
- `/dashboard` is correctly noindexed.
- The sitemap URLs match the public routes and use the same origin as `geo.config.json`.

## Suggested order
1. Fix #1, #2, and #3 first.
2. Then #4 and #5, which are small `robots.txt` edits.
3. Then #6 through #8.

I haven't changed anything. I can implement any of these if you want.
